newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: European Union observers say Pakistani polls fair.
newsitem.headline: European Union observers say Pakistani polls fair.

text.p: A European Union team of election observers said on Tuesday they had found no evidence of widespread electoral fraud in Pakistan's polls.

Pakistanis voted in national and provincial assembly elections -- held on the same day for the first time -- on Monday, handing a convincing win to Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League against Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party.

"The European Union observers believe that, in general, the results of the election expressed the wishes of the Pakistani electorate and the process of voting was transparent in spite of some shortcomings," the EU team said in a statement.
"These for the most part concerned the compilation of electoral registers, the identification of voters and voting by women and minorities...
"The observers found no evidence of widespread electoral fraud."
It said the election authorities in Pakistan had tried hard to create conditions for free and fair voting, although procedural and technical arrangements left room for improvement.
On Monday, the leader of a Commonwealth team of observers, former Australian prime minister Malcolm Fraser, said there had been shortcomings, but not enough to affect the outcome.
